formations.label: Finite attention
formations.description: Only a fraction of available information can be noticed and weighted at once.

formations.label: Reconstructive memory
formations.description: Remembering rebuilds an event from traces, cues and later knowledge rather than replaying an archive.

formations.label: Pattern completion under uncertainty
formations.description: Sparse evidence is completed with familiar patterns, prototypes and causal expectations.

formations.label: Reference points and asymmetric loss
formations.description: Values depend on a comparison point, and losses can carry a different weight from comparable gains.

formations.label: Prior-belief preservation
formations.description: Existing beliefs organise search, interpretation and standards of proof.

formations.label: Self and group protection
formations.description: Judgement can defend identity, esteem, belonging and a favourable account of one's group.

formations.label: Social imitation and coordination
formations.description: Other people's behaviour supplies information, norms and pressure for coordinated action.

formations.label: Action under limited time and computation
formations.description: Choice relies on shortcuts when time, information or computational capacity is limited.

formations.label: Affect, familiarity and processing fluency
formations.description: Feelings and ease of processing can be used as information about liking, risk and truth.

families.label: Attention and salience
families.description: What is vivid, recent, prominent or easy to retrieve receives disproportionate weight.

families.label: Familiarity and affect
families.description: Familiarity, processing ease and feeling colour liking, truth and risk judgements.

families.label: Memory reconstruction
families.description: Later knowledge, present beliefs and source confusion reshape recollection.

families.label: Pattern and probability
families.description: Small samples and resemblance are treated as stronger statistical evidence than they warrant.

families.label: Prior preservation
families.description: Search, scrutiny and recall bend towards an existing belief, hypothesis or desired conclusion.

families.label: Reference dependence
families.description: Anchors, ownership, defaults and prior investment define gains, losses and acceptable change.

families.label: Self-protection
families.description: Beliefs about competence, objectivity and control lean towards a favourable self-account.

families.label: Social alignment
families.description: Consensus, authority, group membership and public norms reshape private judgement.

families.label: Attribution and impression
families.description: Behaviour is converted into explanations about persons, situations and social groups.

families.label: Bounded choice and action
families.description: Choice architecture, delay, ambiguity and action costs shape what people finally do.

mechanisms.label: Finite attention
mechanisms.description: Limited attention leaves some available information unnoticed or underweighted.

mechanisms.label: Salience weighting
mechanisms.description: Prominent, vivid or distinctive information receives extra weight.

mechanisms.label: Associative retrieval
mechanisms.description: Cues make related memories easier to retrieve and use in judgement.

mechanisms.label: Reconstructive memory
mechanisms.description: Recall rebuilds an event using fragments, expectations and later knowledge.

mechanisms.label: Source monitoring
mechanisms.description: People infer where remembered content came from and can misassign its source.

mechanisms.label: Processing fluency
mechanisms.description: Ease of processing is used as information about familiarity, liking or truth.

mechanisms.label: Affect as information
mechanisms.description: Current feelings are treated as evidence about value, risk or the situation.

mechanisms.label: Pattern completion
mechanisms.description: Sparse or noisy observations are completed into a coherent pattern.

mechanisms.label: Representativeness
mechanisms.description: Resemblance to a prototype substitutes for fuller statistical evaluation.

mechanisms.label: Sample-size insensitivity
mechanisms.description: Small samples are expected to resemble populations more closely than they reliably do.

mechanisms.label: Probability simplification
mechanisms.description: Complex probabilities are replaced by simpler impressions of likelihood.

mechanisms.label: Prior-belief preservation
mechanisms.description: Existing beliefs shape search, interpretation, recall and standards of proof.

mechanisms.label: Directional motivation
mechanisms.description: A preferred conclusion influences which reasoning strategies feel persuasive.

mechanisms.label: Reference dependence
mechanisms.description: Evaluation depends on a comparison point rather than only final outcomes.

mechanisms.label: Loss asymmetry
mechanisms.description: Potential losses and comparable gains have unequal psychological weight.

mechanisms.label: Ownership attachment
mechanisms.description: Possession changes the reference point and strengthens attachment to an option.

mechanisms.label: Default inertia
mechanisms.description: The preselected or existing state is retained because changing it has costs or implications.

mechanisms.label: Commitment consistency
mechanisms.description: Past choices and public commitments create pressure to appear consistent.

mechanisms.label: Mental accounting
mechanisms.description: Resources and outcomes are evaluated within separate informal accounts.

mechanisms.label: Self-enhancement
mechanisms.description: Judgement favours interpretations that preserve a positive view of the self.

mechanisms.label: Confidence miscalibration
mechanisms.description: Expressed confidence does not track accuracy as closely as assumed.

mechanisms.label: Control inference
mechanisms.description: Agency or predictability is inferred from cues that may not imply real control.

mechanisms.label: Identity protection
mechanisms.description: Information is interpreted in ways that defend identity, belonging or esteem.

mechanisms.label: Causal attribution
mechanisms.description: Observed behaviour is converted into explanations about persons and situations.

mechanisms.label: Social imitation
mechanisms.description: Other people's behaviour supplies information and a model for one's own response.

mechanisms.label: Norm coordination
mechanisms.description: Perceived expectations and shared rules align behaviour within a group.

mechanisms.label: Authority deference
mechanisms.description: An authority cue increases acceptance or compliance beyond the underlying evidence.

mechanisms.label: In-group protection
mechanisms.description: Judgement favours one's group or protects its identity and reputation.

mechanisms.label: Temporal discounting
mechanisms.description: Outcomes lose subjective weight as their delay increases.

mechanisms.label: Attribute substitution
mechanisms.description: A difficult judgement is answered using an easier, related attribute.

mechanisms.label: Action–omission asymmetry
mechanisms.description: Otherwise similar outcomes are evaluated differently depending on whether action or inaction produced them.
